# Introduction {.unnumbered}

## Why Domain Language Matters

Academic reading in English draws its passages from a limited set of recurring topic worlds（主题世界）: science, environment, life, climate, education, psychology, health, economy, work, cities, agriculture, technology, history, media, design, and culture. These worlds appear across examinations, textbooks, university courses, and public discourse because they represent the domains where educated societies think, investigate, debate, and make decisions.

Each domain has its own way of organising reality — its own conceptual structure（概念结构）, its own network of relationships, and its own language for expressing those relationships. A reader who understands how a domain works can follow a new text in that domain with greater speed and accuracy. A reader who does not must build that understanding from scratch while reading — a slower, more effortful process.

## How This Book Works

This book builds domain knowledge and domain language together, one domain at a time. Each chapter:

1. Opens a topic world and explains how its core concepts connect
2. Introduces the English expressions where they naturally live — inside mechanisms, relationships, and processes
3. Develops the meaning networks（意义网络）that give each term its full explanatory power
4. Uses Chinese brackets to clarify key concepts without interrupting English reading

The writing follows the style of academic texts — English-first exposition with Chinese brackets for key concepts — so that the reader builds comprehension in the same language environment they will encounter in actual reading.

## How to Use This Book

The chapters can be read in order, building domain knowledge progressively across all 15 topic worlds. Alternatively, readers can select the domains most relevant to their interests — a student of environmental science might begin with Chapters 3 and 4, while a student of business might start with Chapters 9 and 10.

Each section within a chapter focuses on one core mechanism. The reader should aim to understand how the mechanism works, how the concepts connect, and how English expresses those connections — rather than memorising individual terms in isolation.

## What This Book Does Not Do

This book does not teach test techniques — skimming, scanning, identifying question types, or eliminating incorrect options. These techniques are valuable, but they work best when comprehension is already present. This book builds the comprehension that makes those techniques effective.

This book does not provide practice exercises or sample questions. These can be developed later as a companion volume or workbook.

This book does not replace the need to read authentic academic texts. It provides the domain foundation（领域基础）that makes reading those texts easier and more productive.
